items.title: UK, Syria pledge to work with allies to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Keir Starmer meets Syrian president in Downing Street amid Middle ...

items.description: As the war between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other enters its fifth week, UN Secretary-General António Guterres has intensified his calls for all parties to pull back from the brink, warning that the conflict has spiraled "out of control" and risks devastating consequences for civilians and the global economy alike. His appeals come as diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — closed by Iran since early March — gain new urgency, with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa pledging on Tuesday to "work with others to restore freedom of navigation" through the critical waterway.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz will 'automatically' reopen when US exits Iran war

featured_image.name: 12 times Trump signaled the Iran war was about to end - Axios

items.description:
President Trump declared Tuesday that the month-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran "won't last much longer" and that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen on its own once American forces withdraw, even as Iran's government flatly denied any negotiations are underway to end the conflict.

In a phone interview with the New York Post published on March 31, Trump framed the U.S. mission narrowly. "My primary responsibility was to ensure they don't possess a nuclear weapon. They will not acquire a nuclear weapon. Once we depart, the strait will automatically open," he said. He added that Iran "has no power remaining" and suggested that countries reliant on the waterway should "take the initiative to open it" themselves.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says US will finish Iran war in 'two to three weeks'

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump estimated on Tuesday that the United States would be finished with its military campaign against Iran in "two to three weeks," the latest in a series of shifting timelines as the conflict enters its second month with no clear exit strategy in sight.[1][2]

The remarks came as the Pentagon deployed B-52 bombers over Iranian airspace for the first time since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28, a move Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine said was possible because U.S. and Israeli forces had dismantled Iran's air defense capabilities to such an extent that the slower aircraft could now operate safely. Trump also signaled a retreat from one of his stated objectives, telling aides he is willing to end the war even if the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply — remains largely closed, according to The Wall Street Journal.[3][4]

items.description: NASA is hours away from launching the first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century, with Navy Captain Victor Glover at the controls. items.title: China verifies Mach 6 engine prototype after 30 years

featured_image.name: China's hypersonic jet shatters Mach 6.5 speed in Gobi desert test

items.description: Chinese researchers have completed and experimentally verified a prototype of a novel air-breathing propulsion system that can accelerate from a dead stop to more than six times the speed of sound, according to a report by the South China Morning Post on Sunday. The engine, called the "contra-rotary ramjet," represents over three decades of development and could reshape the design of future fighter jets and hypersonic missiles.[1][2][3]

items.title: Fourth Greek tanker crosses Hormuz despite Iran blockade

featured_image.name: Oil tanker transits Hormuz in rare voyage after Iran war disruption

items.description:
The Greek-controlled Suezmax tanker Pola has successfully crossed the Strait of Hormuz, becoming the fourth vessel managed by Athens-based Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd. to navigate the chokepoint since the US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on February 28, according to Bloomberg.[1]

The Pola switched off its Automatic Identification System in the Persian Gulf on March 10 and reappeared on Monday in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia's Sumatra island, vessel tracking data compiled by Bloomberg showed. The tanker, laden with roughly 1 million barrels of crude, is en route to Thailand, according to intelligence firm Kpler.[1]

items.title: King Charles confirms first US state visit as monarch

featured_image.name: King Charles to address Congress in historic first state ... - Fox News

items.description:
Buckingham Palace announced on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will undertake a state visit to the United States in late April, marking the first trip to America by a British monarch since Queen Elizabeth II's visit in 2007.[1][2]

The visit, made at the invitation of President Donald Trump and on the advice of the British government, will celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence — a milestone with particular resonance given that the U.S. declared independence during the reign of Charles's ancestor King George III.[2]
